gaps.title: An unidentified voice speaker can steer the owner's running admin turn: busy verbs bypass the speaker-claim clamp and the relay receipt is never consulted on the mid-turn path
gaps.origin_evidence: hermes gateway/run_voice.py:247-257 — _is_user_authorized(source) and duplicate suppression run BEFORE any dispatch, including the busy-path steer that run_inbound.py:560-596 performs; hermes plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py:3640 gates each speaker before STT. openclaw src/channels/message-access/sender-gates.ts:55-125 — the sender gate runs at ingress for every message, and talk/agent-consult-runtime.ts:44-50 forwards senderIsOwner from that boundary into every consult.
gaps.halbert_evidence: dashboard/routes/agent.py:1697-1700 calls agent.handle_midturn_arrival(session_id, request.message, channel=channel) BEFORE the receipt is consumed at 1794-1802, so on the steer path stamped_voice_fields never runs; agents/state_machine.py:1793-1807 decides steer from channel.busy_verbs alone (no claim, no role); 1848-1850 request_steer(text); 1751-1756 the steered text is appended to self.ctx (the running turn, whose speaker_role/claim are the owner's from routes/agent.py:1786-1803 and state_machine.py:551-560). tools/role_gate.py:169-194 effective_voice_role is consulted only via current_turn_claim bound for the running turn, i.e. the owner's ASSERTED claim, not the steerer's.
gaps.failure_scenario: The owner types 'clean up the old snapshots on tank' in the dashboard and walks away; the turn is EXECUTING. A guest in the room (no enrolled voiceprint) says 'and delete the backups on the external drive too'. The mic uplink is the owner's authenticated socket, the pipeline emits an unidentified observation, VoiceMode auto-submits it with modality=voice; the route resolves the voice channel, whose busy_verbs contains steer, and handle_midturn_arrival steers the text into the running turn before any receipt/role stamping. The guest's words now ride an admin-role turn with the owner's ASSERTED claim bound, so the RoleGate cap for unknown speakers (the whole point of default_role=unknown) never applies. Had the same guest spoken while the machine was idle, the turn would have run at role unknown and been capped.
gaps.proposed_test: tests/test_channel_registry.py (or test_voice_relay_honest.py): start a slow turn via agent.process(query=..., session_id='owner', speaker_role='admin', claim_source='dashboard_token'); while it is in flight POST /api/agent/message with modality='voice' and no relay_token (and separately with a receipt whose verified=False) and text 'delete the backups too'. Assert the response is NOT steer_accepted (expect a typed refusal/degrade event or a queued turn at role unknown), and that agent.ctx.observations contains no '[steered] delete the backups too'. A second case: a receipt with verified=True and speaker_role='admin' steers. A third: the receipt is consumed (store.consume(token) is None) whichever branch ran.
gaps.proposed_fix: In routes/agent.py move the receipt consumption + stamped_voice_fields block above the handle_midturn_arrival call and pass the stamped role/claim strength into it; in state_machine.handle_midturn_arrival require, for a channel whose default_role is not admin, that the arrival's claim strength meets the running turn's role floor (claim_from_source(stamped).strength >= ASSERTED and stated role >= self.ctx.speaker_role by ROLE_MAX_RISK order) before steer/stop are honoured — otherwise degrade to queue (a fresh turn at role unknown) with a new typed verdict event (e.g. steer_declined reason='claim_below_running_turn'). Deterministic policy only; no model involved. Engine-side: none.

verdict.reason: ORIGIN read and confirmed, stronger than the audit claimed. hermes gateway/run_voice.py:251 `if not self._is_user_authorized(source): return` and :254 `_is_duplicate_voice_transcript(...)` both run before the synthetic MessageEvent is built at :273-276 and dispatched at :277 `await adapter.handle_message(event)`. The busy/steer path is behind the SAME gate with an explicit incident comment: gateway/run_busy.py:652-663 `_handle_active_session_busy_message` -> '# Same authorization gate as the cold path, else unauthorized users in shared threads inject messages into a session they don't own. # See #17775.' + `if not self._is_user_authorized(event.source)` -> silent drop; the steer itself is downstream at gateway/run_inbound.py:553-567 `_hm_busy_steer`. OpenClaw corroborates: src/talk/agent-consult-runtime.ts:43-49 'Ingress owns authentication; consumers that require this handoff must fail closed on other revisions.'; src/channels/message-access/sender-gates.ts:53-124 senderGateForDirect blocks at ingress. HALBERT confirmed on the cited lines and by whole-core grep: dashboard/routes/agent.py:1693-1696 calls `agent.handle_midturn_arrival(session_id, request.message, channel=channel)` and returns the arrival stream at 1697-1711, while the receipt is only consumed at 1794-1801 (`get_voice_relay_receipts().consume(request.relay_token)` / `stamped_voice_fields`) — so on the steer path stamped_voice_fields never runs. agents/state_machine.py:1783-1846 decides the verb from `channel.busy_verbs` alone; agents/channels.py:91-99 VOICE_CHANNEL busy_verbs={'steer'}, default_role='unknown'. request_steer (state_machine.py:1702-1726) writes into `self._pending_steer[self.ctx.session_id]` — the RUNNING turn's id — and _drain_pending_steer (1728-1756) appends into that turn's `ctx.observations`, whose speaker_role/claim were bound at state_machine.py:551-560 and 634-635 from the OWNER's dashboard turn (admin, uncapped). No claim/role/receipt check exists on that path anywhere: grep of handle_midturn_arrival across core, tests and .handoff shows only busy-verb tests (tests/agents/test_busy_mode_unification.py:84-190) and route fakes returning the idle branch (tests/test_voice_ingress.py:61-70, tests/test_channel_registry.py:315-317), so the mid-turn voice path is untested. Reachability verified end-to-end: dashboard/frontend/src/pages/VoiceMode.tsx:305-309 auto-submits every relayed transcript with only relayToken, and the mic stays armed in listening/recognized/interrupted (VoiceMode.tsx:335-341). No doc records a decision to leave this open. High stands: it defeats the exact control VOICE_CHANNEL.default_role='unknown' + tools/role_gate.py:169-196 effective_voice_role exist for.

gaps.title: No duplicate-transcript suppression: one utterance can become two or more turns
gaps.origin_evidence: hermes gateway/run_voice.py:205-221 _is_duplicate_voice_transcript — normalized text, 12s window, exact or SequenceMatcher>=0.95 for >=16 chars, keyed per (guild,user), last 5 kept; invoked at 254-257 before dispatch. Hermes docstring at 206-207 gives the reason: 'voice capture can emit it twice a few seconds apart -> a second queued run and overlapping spoken replies'.
gaps.halbert_evidence: No suppression anywhere: grep for SequenceMatcher / duplicate transcript / recent transcripts over audio/, dashboard/, integrations/, agents/ returns nothing. audio/pipeline.py:376-382 fires _process_speech_segment on every speech-positive frame while IDLE and 398 re-reads the last 10s of the shared ring buffer (which still contains the previous utterance after the turn returns to IDLE at 462). app.py:1476-1482 broadcasts to every connected uplink socket (webrtc_ingress.py:111-113 loops over all sockets) and pages/VoiceMode.tsx:302-311 auto-submits every transcript it receives. The receipt is single-use (voice_relay.py:144-145) so the second submission is unidentified, but it still runs as a full turn. PACKET-04 addendum item 5 (.handoff/OPENCLAW-LIFT-PACKET-04-VOICE-INGRESS-2026-09-07.md:201) called for this and it was not built.
gaps.failure_scenario: Owner says 'restart the media server'. VAD fires, the last 10s are transcribed, a receipt is minted, the browser submits the turn. The pipeline returns to IDLE at pipeline.py:462 while the tail of the same utterance is still arriving in the chunk queue; the next speech-positive frame re-reads the ring (which still holds 'restart the media server') and emits a second observation with the same text. The relay mints a second receipt and broadcasts again; VoiceMode submits a second turn 'restart the media server' — now unidentified (role unknown) — which queues behind the first (state_machine.py:500-510 turn_queued) and restarts the service a second time, or is refused by the RoleGate and produces a confusing second spoken answer. With the /voice page and the floating HUD both holding an uplink, every utterance is doubled unconditionally.
gaps.proposed_test: tests/test_voice_relay_honest.py: feed _relay_voice_turn (or a new dedupe seam in voice_relay.py) two observations with text 'restart the media server' and 'Restart the media server.' 3s apart (monkeypatched clock) and assert the second broadcasts nothing and mints no receipt; a third observation 13s later broadcasts. Also assert a different text within the window is NOT suppressed, and that texts shorter than 16 chars require exact normalized equality.
gaps.proposed_fix: Add a deterministic suppressor to dashboard/voice_relay.py (normalize: whitespace collapse, punctuation strip, lower; window 12s; exact or difflib.SequenceMatcher ratio>=0.95 when min length>=16; ring of 5) and call it in app.py _relay_voice_turn before record(). Key by observation.speaker_id or '' (one household). Additionally give each receipt an observation id in the broadcast so a second uplink socket redeeming the same observation is recognised server-side as a duplicate submission rather than an unidentified new turn (route: if the token is already spent AND the text equals the spent receipt's text within TTL, answer with a typed 'duplicate_utterance' event instead of running a turn — requires keeping spent tokens' text hash for the TTL). Engine-side: none.

verdict.reason: ORIGIN confirmed verbatim: hermes gateway/run_voice.py:205-221 `_is_duplicate_voice_transcript` — docstring 'voice capture can emit it twice a few seconds apart -> a second queued run and overlapping spoken replies', punctuation/whitespace/lower normalization, 12.0s window, `prior == normalized or (min(len) >= 16 and SequenceMatcher(...).ratio() >= 0.95)`, ring `[-5:]` keyed (guild_id, user_id); invoked at :254-257 before dispatch at :277. HALBERT lacks it: grep for SequenceMatcher/difflib/duplicate over audio/, dashboard/voice_relay.py and integrations/ finds nothing relevant. Mechanism verified independently: audio/pipeline.py:376-382 fires `_process_speech_segment` on any speech-positive frame while state==IDLE; :391-398 reads `read_last_seconds(10.0)`; audio/buffer.py:90-114 `read_window` is a NON-CONSUMING peek backward from _write_pos, so the prior utterance is still in the window; pipeline.py:462 returns to IDLE immediately after the callback, so the next VAD onset re-transcribes the same audio. dashboard/app.py:1467-1482 mints a fresh receipt and broadcasts per observation; VoiceMode.tsx:305-309 auto-submits each. .handoff/OPENCLAW-LIFT-PACKET-04-VOICE-INGRESS-2026-09-07.md:201 addendum item 5 explicitly called for this and it was not built — intent to port, not a decision against. TWO AUDIT CORRECTIONS (why medium, not high): (a) 'every utterance is doubled with the /voice page and the floating HUD both holding an uplink' is WRONG — grep onTranscript over dashboard/frontend/src finds only lib/pcmCapture.ts:227/392 and pages/VoiceMode.tsx; no HUD consumes transcripts; (b) the second submission carries a NEW valid receipt (app.py:1474 records a fresh observation), so it is NOT unidentified — it runs at the same identified role as the first, making double-execution more likely than the audit's version, not less.

gaps.title: No STT hallucination filter: silence/TV can produce 'Thank you.' turns
gaps.origin_evidence: hermes plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py:3663 `if not transcript or is_whisper_hallucination(transcript): return` before the voice callback; tools/voice_mode_transcript.py:20-40 phrase set (multi-language) + _HALLUCINATION_REPEAT_RE; tools/transcription_local.py:152-215 Silero VAD, condition_on_previous_text=False, per-segment no_speech_prob/avg_logprob gate; tests/tools/test_stt_silence_hallucinations.py:75-135 pin the gate.
gaps.halbert_evidence: audio/pipeline.py:407-414 after ASR the only gate is `if not text`; app.py:1466-1468 only `if not text.strip()`; grep hallucin over audio/ finds only asr_engine.py:87 rule3_min_utterance_length (an endpointing constant). pipeline.py:398 transcribes a fixed 10s window regardless of how much of it is speech, so a mostly-silent window reaches the ASR whenever a single VAD frame fires (pipeline.py:368-382).
gaps.failure_scenario: The TV is on in the room (privacy.ignore_tv_media is a config flag on routes/audio.py:95 but the speech track has no content gate). A laugh track trips VAD once; the 10s window is mostly room noise; the ASR returns 'Thank you.' The relay mints a receipt and broadcasts, VoiceMode auto-submits 'Thank you.' as a voice turn, the agent answers aloud ('You're welcome'), the speaker output re-enters the mic (no AEC unless local_mic.aec_enabled), VAD fires again, and the loop repeats every few seconds until someone taps the page. Each cycle is a persisted user row in the one continuous conversation.

gaps.title: Tee payloads carry no monotonic sequence, no timestamp and no turn-id assertion, so a second screen cannot detect gaps or order after a reconnect
gaps.origin_evidence: openclaw src/talk/talk-events.ts:143-177 every event gets seq (monotonic per session), id=`${sessionId}:${seq}`, timestamp, and the session context copied on; 105-141 turn-scoped events without a turnId throw; talk-events.test.ts:6 and :79 pin both.
gaps.halbert_evidence: agents/turn_event_tee.py:116-133 publish fans the dict out as given; agents/state_machine.py:3826-3831 builds {event, session_id, channel, **fields} with no seq/timestamp and accepts session_id='' silently (3832-3833 swallows all errors); dashboard/app.py:1023-1032 the /ws bridge drops the event when no loop is running ('the tee is observation, never delivery').
gaps.failure_scenario: The floating voice HUD reconnects its /ws while the dashboard turn is in EXECUTING. It receives tool_complete then state_change(RESPONDING) but missed tool_start and turn_started; with no seq it cannot tell that it joined mid-turn versus that the events arrived out of order, and with no timestamp it cannot age out a stale 'thinking' indicator after a dropped turn_ended (the bridge drops on RuntimeError). The HUD shows 'thinking' indefinitely.
gaps.proposed_test: tests/test_turn_event_tee.py: publish three events for one session and assert payload['seq'] is 1,2,3 and payload['ts'] is monotonic; assert publish of a turn-scoped event with session_id='' is refused (logged, not delivered) rather than fanned out.
gaps.proposed_fix: In TurnEventTee.publish stamp seq (per process, monotonic int) and ts (time.time()) onto the cleaned payload before fan-out; in _tee_publish skip (debug-log) when session_id is falsy for the turn-scoped names. Frontend HUD consumer can then reset on a seq regression. Engine-side: none.

verdict.reason: ORIGIN confirmed: openclaw src/talk/talk-events.ts:144-176 `createTalkEventSequencer` stamps `id: `${context.sessionId}:${seq}``, monotonic `seq` and `timestamp` (injectable clock) on every event; :106-140 TURN_SCOPED_TALK_EVENT_TYPES + assertTalkEventCorrelation throws `Talk event ${type} requires turnId`. Both test-pinned: src/talk/talk-events.test.ts:6-19 ('adds stable session context and monotonically increasing sequence numbers', id 'session-1:1') and :79-90 ('rejects turn and capture scoped events without correlation ids'). HALBERT confirmed lacking: agents/turn_event_tee.py:116-133 `publish` fans the payload out as given — no seq, no ts, no correlation assertion; agents/state_machine.py:3821-3833 `_tee_publish` emits `{'event', 'session_id', 'channel', **fields}`, accepts an empty session_id silently and swallows all exceptions at 3832-3833. The /ws bridge at dashboard/app.py:1022-1032 drops on RuntimeError ('the tee is observation, never delivery') and ConnectionManager.broadcast (app.py:868-886) adds no envelope fields, so a reconnecting consumer cannot detect the drop. APPLIES: not multi-tenant machinery — app.py:1009-1019 names the voice HUD 'and any second screen in the room' as the tee's reason to exist, which is exactly the reconnect case; the 'observation, never delivery' stance argues FOR a sequence number, not against. Low is right: no security consequence, a stuck 'thinking' indicator at worst.

gaps.title: The voice relay is bound after the speech loop is already live, so an utterance completing in the boot window is silently dropped
gaps.origin_evidence: hermes gateway/run_voice.py:147-148 — '# Wire callbacks BEFORE join so voice input arriving right after connection is not lost.' _bind_voice_input_callback(adapter) precedes adapter.join_voice_channel.
gaps.halbert_evidence: dashboard/app.py:1385 `await coordinator.start()` (pipeline.py:172 creates the speech track task) and :1388 set_audio_pipeline precede :1484 `_coordinator.on_voice_turn = _relay_voice_turn`; between them run the acoustic bridge and other startup work. audio/pipeline.py:456-460 `if self.on_voice_turn:` — an observation emitted while it is None goes nowhere and no log line records it.
gaps.failure_scenario: The dashboard restarts while the owner's /voice page is open with an active uplink (pcmCapture reconnects). The owner speaks as the server comes up; the ingress accepts frames the instant the coordinator starts, the speech track transcribes, and the observation is dropped because the relay is not yet bound. The page's 8s recognition watchdog shows a neutral note and the owner repeats themselves. Rare, but the origin ordered the binding explicitly to close exactly this.
gaps.proposed_test: tests/test_voice_ingress.py TestRelayRegressionPin: AST-check that in app.py the assignment to on_voice_turn occurs (by line) before the `await coordinator.start()` call; or restructure so the relay is a constructor argument to AudioPipelineCoordinator and assert the coordinator never starts with on_voice_turn None.

Engine-side: none.

verdict.reason: ORIGIN confirmed verbatim: hermes gateway/run_voice.py:147-148 '# Wire callbacks BEFORE join so voice input arriving right after connection is not lost.' then `self._bind_voice_input_callback(adapter)`, with `await adapter.join_voice_channel(...)` only at :160. The Halbert ordering claim is literally true — dashboard/app.py:1395 `await coordinator.start()` precedes :1484 `_coordinator.on_voice_turn = _relay_voice_turn`. REFUTED because the failure cannot occur. The coordinator has exactly ONE ingress (`grep -rn add_ingress` over core: only dashboard/app.py:1387 attaching `WebRtcIngress(area_id='dashboard_voice')`, plus the definition at audio/pipeline.py:207), and that ingress produces audio ONLY from browser WebSocket frames: audio/ingress/webrtc_ingress.py:47-61 `start()` just sets a flag and logs 'WebSocket endpoint is registered separately'; frames enter only via :63-92 `handle_websocket` -> `await websocket.receive_bytes()`. Both the start() and the on_voice_turn assignment run inside the SAME ASGI lifespan startup block (app.py:1374-1486 under `if _caps.has(CAP_AUDIO)`), and uvicorn accepts no connection — including the /api/audio/stream upgrade — until lifespan startup completes, so no frame (and no ring-buffer content) can exist while on_voice_turn is None. No local-mic or Wyoming ingress is attached at startup (`grep -rn on_voice_turn` over core: only app.py:1484 and pipeline.py:92/108/456/458/570/572). The audit's 'Rare' understates it: unreachable, not rare. A warning log at pipeline.py:456-460 for a consumer-less observation would still be cheap, but this is not a gap against the origin.

halbert_own_bugs.verdict_reason: Confirmed exactly as cited. agents/state_machine.py:546-560: `normalized_modality = str(modality or '').strip().lower()`; `if normalized_modality in ('voice','terminal'): turn_modality = normalized_modality else: turn_modality = 'text'`; then `turn_speaker_role = resolve_channel(turn_modality).default_role` -> DASHBOARD_CHANNEL.default_role == 'admin' (channels.py:78-85), with channel provenance bound to 'dashboard' at 573-577. agents/channels.py:170-196 resolve_channel raises ChannelRefused otherwise, and its docstring at 180-183 does claim 'Normalization matches process()'s own, so the route and the state machine can never disagree' — false for a fourth value: the route refuses (routes/agent.py:1668-1675) but process() coerces to admin. halbert_own_bugs.title: Relay receipt is orphaned on the mid-turn path and the steer carries no speaker provenance
halbert_own_bugs.evidence: routes/agent.py:1697-1700 handle_midturn_arrival returns before the receipt is consumed at 1794-1802; voice_relay.py:135-149 the receipt therefore stays pending for TTL_S=300; state_machine.py:1848-1870 steer_accepted carries only replaced/demoted flags; 1751-1756 the observation line is '[steered] {text}' with no speaker.
halbert_own_bugs.scenario: Owner's turn is running; the enrolled owner speaks a correction. The steer is applied (correct) but the receipt is never spent, so the same token + same words remain redeemable for five minutes; the thread row and the tee show a steer with no speaker, so the audit trail cannot say who corrected the running turn. (The security consequence — an unverified speaker steering — is G1; this entry is the bookkeeping half.)
halbert_own_bugs.verdict_reason: Both halves confirmed. (a) routes/agent.py:1693-1711 returns the arrival StreamingResponse before reaching the consume() at 1794-1801, so `consume(request.relay_token)` never runs for a steer; dashboard/voice_relay.py:135-149 `consume` is the only place a token is popped, and record() at :120-134 leaves it in `self._pending` until TTL_S expiry or ring eviction at MAX_ENTRIES — the token plus the same words stay redeemable for the TTL (stamped_voice_fields binds the receipt to the exact transcript at :190-196, so the replay is confined to that utterance). (b) state_machine.py:1847-1866 the steer_accepted tee payload and StreamEvent carry only {reason, replaced, demoted}, and _drain_pending_steer at 1755 writes `ctx.add_observation(f'[steered] {text}')` with no speaker field. Bookkeeping/audit defect as described; the security half is G1.

halbert_own_bugs.title: weakest_claim([]) raises ValueError where the origin function is total
halbert_own_bugs.evidence: persona/claims.py:64-66 `return min(claims, key=...)`; openclaw identifier-authentication.ts:21-29 takes exactly two claims and always returns one. No production caller today (grep weakest_claim( over halbert_core: only the definition).

Origin comparison confirmed: openclaw src/channels/message-access/identifier-authentication.ts:21-28 `weakestIdentifierAuthentication(entry, subject)` takes exactly two named claims and always returns one — total by construction. `grep -rn weakest_claim` over the whole Halbert repo returns only the definition and tests/persona/test_claims.py:4/15/17 — NO production caller, so there is no live failure path. halbert_own_bugs.title: A matcher hit whose profile lookup fails is recorded as a verified claim with no subject
halbert_own_bugs.evidence: audio/pipeline.py:421-435 sets speaker_id from the match before `store.get(speaker_id)`; if the profile is missing, speaker_name stays '' and speaker_role 'unknown' but speaker_id is set; voice_relay.py:74-79 `_verified_from_observation` = bool(speaker_id); 199-204 then stamps claim_source='voice_speaker_verification' (ASSERTED) with speaker_name None; routes/audio.py:293-299 a delete whose live-matcher remove() fails leaves exactly this state until restart.
halbert_own_bugs.scenario: The owner deletes a former housemate's voiceprint; live_identifier.remove raises (logged at warning, audio.py:299). The housemate visits and speaks: the running matcher still returns their old speaker_id, the store has no profile, the receipt records verified=True/role 'unknown', and the turn carries an ASSERTED speaker claim with value_sha256=''. Role stays 'unknown' so nothing is granted, but the audit log (state_machine.py:728-735 claim_strength=asserted) says a verified speaker spoke when the server cannot say who.
halbert_own_bugs.verdict_reason: Full chain read and confirmed. audio/pipeline.py:421-441: `match = self._speaker_id.identify(pcm)`; `speaker_id = match.speaker_id` is set FIRST, then `profile = store.get(speaker_id)` and only `if profile:` fills name/role — a missing profile leaves speaker_id set, name '' and role 'unknown'. dashboard/voice_relay.py:74-79 `_verified_from_observation` returns `bool(getattr(observation,'speaker_id','') or '')` — verified=True on the id alone. voice_relay.py:198-203 `if receipt.verified: return ('voice_speaker_verification', receipt.speaker_name or None, receipt.speaker_role or None)` -> ('voice_speaker_verification', None, None), which persona/claims.py:44-57 maps to an ASSERTED IdentifierClaim with `value_sha256=''`. Delete race real: dashboard/routes/audio.py:283-300 — store.delete() succeeds, then a `live_identifier.remove(speaker_id)` failure is only logged at warning ('Speaker %s deleted but still in the live matcher'), leaving this state until restart. No privilege is granted (role stays 'unknown'; role_gate.py:169-196 only caps, never lifts), so the harm is audit dishonesty: state_machine.py:728-735 logs claim_strength=asserted for a speaker the server cannot name.

halbert_own_bugs.title: The speech track reads the 10s window at speech ONSET, not after end-of-speech
halbert_own_bugs.evidence: audio/pipeline.py:368-382 on the first speech-positive frame while IDLE it awaits _process_speech_segment immediately; 391-398 that function reads `await self._ring_buffer.read_last_seconds(10.0)` with no wait for silence; hermes plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py:860 check_silence accumulates until silence and tests/gateway/test_voice_command.py:461-486 pin 'returns completed utterance' / 'ignores short buffer'. (Adjacent to the listed unit files; it is the producer of every observation the relay stamps.)
halbert_own_bugs.scenario: Owner presses push-to-talk and says 'what is using port 8080'. The first 32ms speech frame trips VAD; the ASR is handed the previous ~10s of near-silence plus 32ms of 'wh'. Either the transcript is empty (turn dropped, watchdog note) or a hallucinated fragment is relayed with a receipt (G3). Only a streaming ASR that keeps consuming while THINKING could make this work, and pipeline.py:406 calls transcribe_chunk(pcm) once on the snapshot. This may be masked in practice by the ring buffer having been filled by the user's speech on a slower VAD onset, but the code as written transcribes before the utterance ends.
halbert_own_bugs.verdict_reason: Confirmed, with extra corroboration. audio/pipeline.py:376-382: on the first speech-positive frame while state==IDLE (wake_detected defaults True) it immediately `await self._process_speech_segment(...)`; :391-398 its first act is `pcm = await self._ring_buffer.read_last_seconds(10.0)` with no wait for a silence run, and :406 calls `self._asr.transcribe_chunk(pcm)` once on that snapshot. audio/buffer.py:90-114 confirms read_window is a backward peek from _write_pos — the window is the ten seconds BEFORE the onset frame, not after it. Extra evidence the audit did not cite: asr_engine.py:133-137 transcribe_chunk's own docstring reads 'Synchronous single-chunk transcription (for testing). ... Not suitable for streaming — use transcribe_stream for that' — production is on the test-only entry point while the real streaming API (asr_engine.py:94-131, with is_endpoint/reset) goes unused. Origin contrast confirmed in shape: hermes accumulates until silence before transcribing (plugins/platforms/discord/adapter.py, feeding the transcribe at :3657-3663). This is the root cause under both G2 (overlapping windows -> duplicate transcripts) and the G3 residual; dispatch it as the primary fix, dedupe as the belt.

A09-channels-voice-ingress.summary: The channel registry, server-stamped claim clamp, relay receipts (single-use, TTL, transcript-bound), the D-6 role cap and the observe-only tee are solid and in several places stronger than either origin (fail-closed UNVERIFIED default, receipt-bound identity, echo-guard seam on the tee). The port is weaker than the origins in what happens to a voice transcript BEFORE and BESIDE the stamp: (1) high — the busy-verb path is decided from channel.busy_verbs alone before the receipt is consumed, so an unidentified speaker in the room can steer the owner's running admin turn, defeating the unknown-speaker cap; (2) medium — no duplicate-transcript suppression although the pipeline re-reads the same 10s ring window on every VAD onset and every uplink socket auto-submits; (3) medium — no silence-hallucination filter, so 'Thank you.' from a TV becomes a persisted turn and a spoken reply. Lower: tee payloads carry no seq/timestamp, the relay is bound after the speech loop starts, and no wake-name rule exists for a shared room. Own bugs: process() maps an unknown modality to a typed admin turn (the route refuses it), the tee scrubs only flat strings, weakest_claim is not total, a matcher hit with a missing profile stamps a subject-less ASSERTED claim, and the speech track transcribes the window at speech onset rather than after end-of-speech. All fixes are deterministic and Halbert-side; no engine (Haloysius) implications. gaps.title: No operator control over the catalog rung: the live probe cannot be disabled and there is no 'utility = my chat model, no heuristics' state
gaps.origin_evidence: Hermes agent/auxiliary_client.py:785-792 (_FAST_MODEL_TASKS + auxiliary.<task>.prefer_fast_model, default False; tests/hermes_cli/test_aux_config.py:37, tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client.py:4978-4986); OpenClaw src/agents/utility-model.ts:16-29, 85-87 (explicit empty string = disabled; test 75-81)
gaps.halbert_evidence: model/utility_slot.py:93-97, 127-133 (prefer_fast is a code kwarg); integrations/speech_summarizer.py:102-106 (hardcoded prefer_fast=True); llm_config.py:139-140, 238-246 (empty slot == auto; no disabled tri-state)
gaps.failure_scenario: Single macOS host, chat slot pinned to a local 32B model on Ollama, several small same-family tags also pulled for experiments. Every long spoken reply now runs on whichever 0.5B/1B sibling the ladder finds, producing poor summaries. The operator wants 'always summarize with my chat model' — the only recourse is to pin utility_model to the chat model by hand (which the picker UI does not offer, llm_config.py:24-25) or delete the small tags from Ollama. There is no models.yml key that turns the probe off.
gaps.proposed_test: tests/test_utility_slot.py: write models.yml with chat=family-a:32b, utility_model unset, and a top-level `utility: {prefer_fast: false}` (or `utility_model: {enabled: false, model: "", auto: false}`); monkeypatch _fetch_catalog to pytest.fail; assert _resolve_aux(prefer_fast=True) returns (chat, AuxSource.CHAT). Second test: the operator opt-in absent → today's behaviour preserved only when the caller passes prefer_fast and config allows it.
gaps.proposed_fix: Make the probe an operator opt-in gated in config as Hermes does: `prefer_fast` becomes 'caller asks AND config allows' (`utility_model.catalog_pick: bool`, default false, read via llm_config.load_file()). Optionally add a tri-state on the slot (unset=auto, enabled pin, explicit `auto: false` = chat floor only) mirroring OpenClaw's unset/explicit/disabled. Deterministic, name-neutral, degenerates to one user.

gaps.failure_scenario: Ollama is stopped or the LM Studio endpoint is asleep while the operator is talking to Halbert through a still-reachable peer/secure slot. Every long spoken reply resolves the utility model with prefer_fast=True, blocks up to 2 s (Ollama) or 4 s (two-path generic) on the probe, then falls to the chat floor — and does it again on the next reply. Because the summarizer runs inline in the async responding handler (state_machine.py:4160-4163) the whole event loop stalls for that time on each reply.
gaps.proposed_test: tests/test_utility_slot.py: monkeypatch _fetch_catalog with a counting stub that raises OSError; call _resolve_aux(prefer_fast=True) three times within one second; assert the stub was called once (negative cache) and each call returned the chat floor. Second test: stub returns a catalog; three calls → one fetch; monkeypatch time.monotonic past the TTL → second fetch.
gaps.proposed_fix: Add a per-(url, provider) memo in utility_slot: (entries, monotonic) with a success TTL (e.g. 300 s, the Hermes _ENDPOINT_MODEL_CACHE_TTL) and a failure TTL (e.g. 120 s) storing an empty listing; expose invalidate_catalog_cache() for tests and for llm_config._write_raw to call. gaps.origin_evidence: Hermes agent/auxiliary_client.py:757-766 (policy-blind rungs are re-checked against the provider policy and dropped when blocked); OpenClaw src/agents/utility-model.ts:102-110 (derived default must inherit the primary's isolation; test 93-101)
gaps.halbert_evidence: model/utility_slot.py:93-147, 170-207 (no is_local_model / is_cloud_tagged check on any rung; no require_local parameter); llm_config.py:504-519 (SEC-21 locality enforced only for secure_model at normalise); agents/state_machine.py:4143-4163 (summarizer invoked with no secure_context check; secure_context is tracked at 2565-2571 and used at 2625/3606/3943/3968 but not here); integrations/speech_summarizer.py:100-133
gaps.failure_scenario: Secure turn (secure_context=True) answered by the local secure model. Voice modality on, reply > 600 chars. The ladder runs with prefer_fast=True: the declared utility_model points at the operator's OpenAI-compatible endpoint (allowed — normalise only checks chat-capability, llm_config.py:498-503), or Ollama's /api/tags lists a same-family ':cloud' tag with a smaller parameter_size than the local anchor. The full reply of the secure turn is POSTed to the cloud for summarization. SEC-21's rule ('a :cloud model on localhost is a cloud model', llm_config.py:143-164) is enforced at the picker and the turn gate but not on this side channel.
gaps.proposed_test: tests/test_utility_slot.py: (a) chat=family-a:32b local; catalog = [family-a:3b-cloud-tagged entry (name endswith ':cloud'), family-a:8b]; _resolve_aux(prefer_fast=True, require_local=True) → family-a:8b, never the cloud tag. (b) utility_model declared on an endpoint at https://api.example.com provider openai; _resolve_aux(require_local=True) → skips DECLARED and floors on secure_model (or None), source != DECLARED. (c) tests/test_speech_summarizer.py: with secure_context=True and a resolver stub returning a non-local model, the summarizer speaks the original and never calls call_llm_chat.
gaps.proposed_fix: Add `require_local: bool = False` to resolve_aux_model/_resolve_aux; when set, every rung's candidate must pass llm_config.is_local_model(model, url, provider) (declared, catalog entries, legacy, floor) and the floor becomes secure_model before chat_model. make_speech_summarizer takes `secure: bool` and the state machine passes self.ctx.secure_context; when no local utility model resolves on a secure turn, speak the original. Deterministic, one policy pipeline, no LLM in the decision.

verdict.reason: ORIGIN VERIFIED: auxiliary_client.py:757-766 re-checks a policy-blind aux pick against the provider policy and returns '' when blocked, with the comment 'Rungs 2-4 are policy-blind; a blocked pick is refused at request time, so drop it and let the caller keep the main model'; OpenClaw src/agents/utility-model.ts:102-110 carries the primary's trailing auth profile onto the derived default precisely so 'profile-isolated setups' do not route utility calls through default credentials, pinned by utility-model.test.ts:93-101. HALBERT VERIFIED, and the asymmetry is sharper than the audit states: the main turn's secure gate exists and fails closed (dashboard/routes/agent.py:556, 626-678 'Force a secure turn onto a local endpoint or fail closed', :807 the guide must itself be local), llm_config.py:504-519 disables a non-local secure_model at normalise, and state_machine.py:2565-2571/2625/3606/3943/3968 threads secure=self.ctx.secure_context into every model call -- but state_machine.py:4160-4163 constructs make_speech_summarizer(self.ctx.session_id) with no secure argument, speech_summarizer.py:93-133 has no locality check, utility_slot.py:93-207 has no is_local_model call on any rung, and model/client.py:283-330 enforces nothing beyond CHAT_CAPABLE_PROVIDERS (which includes anthropic and every OpenAI-compatible provider, client.py:75-77), so a declared cloud utility_model passes normalise (llm_config.py:488-503 checks only endpoint existence + chat capability). The catalog path is equally live: executed against the module, _family_token('gpt-oss:20b-cloud') == 'gpt-oss' and estimate_model_params_b == 20.0, so a ':cloud' tag is a legal 'smaller sibling' of a larger local anchor even though llm_config.is_cloud_tagged/is_local_model (llm_config.py:165-216) exist to forbid exactly that. Only partial mitigation: the echo guard (state_machine.py:3764-3805, applied at :4018) redacts the committed reply, but only when it matches previously-egressed material -- it is not a locality guarantee. No test and no .handoff doc records a decision to omit this.

gaps.title: No size floor, no context screening, and tie order unpinned in the 'smallest sibling' rule
gaps.origin_evidence: Hermes agent/auxiliary_client.py:645-651 (families chosen from measured titling latency), 662-668 + 720-729 (deterministic recency ordering; tests 4924-4939), 3863-3912 (context-window screening of fallback candidates)

gaps.proposed_test: tests/test_utility_slot.py: catalog [32b, 0.5b, 3b] with a configurable floor → 3b picked; catalog with two 3B entries in reversed order across two runs → same pick (name tie-break). Optional: entry with context_length < needed is skipped when a min_context kwarg is passed.

verdict.reason: ORIGIN PARTLY VERIFIED: the determinism half holds -- auxiliary_client.py:661-669 _model_recency_key and :717 `ids = sorted(..., key=_model_recency_key, reverse=True)` give a total, deterministic order, pinned by tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client.py:4924-4939; the context-screening half holds -- :3863-3912 (_task_minimum_context_length / _candidate_context_window / _context_too_small) screens fallback candidates, though only the 'compression' task has a floor. The 'size floor' half does NOT exist in the origin: Hermes has a curated family list, not a min_params_b. HALBERT: utility_slot.py:188-202 does admit any strictly-smaller sibling with no minimum and keeps the first listed on a tie, and there is no name tie-break -- that part stands. But the audit's context sub-claim is wrong: model/client.py:731-735 computes num_ctx from the actual prompt (`options.get('num_ctx') or num_ctx_for_model(...)`) and warns loudly at :746-753 when it would truncate, so the summarizer's omission of num_ctx does not cause the described truncation on any local provider. Low: what remains is a quality preference (a 0.5B pick) and an unpinned tie order between two same-size quantisations, both inconsequential and neither test-pinned in the origin as a floor.

gaps.title: Ollama catalog probe is unauthenticated even when the saved endpoint carries an api_key
gaps.origin_evidence: Hermes agent/auxiliary_client.py:682-700 ('Most /v1/models endpoints are authenticated; an anonymous 401 would read as no small model and pin the curated default forever'); tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client.py:4941-4958
gaps.halbert_evidence: model/utility_slot.py:225-229 (GET {base}/api/tags with no headers) vs 231 (Bearer only on the generic path); model/client.py:527-528, 568-569 (Halbert's own Ollama calls DO send Authorization when api_key is set)
gaps.failure_scenario: The operator fronts Ollama with a token-checking reverse proxy on loopback (saved endpoint api_key set). Chat works; the utility probe 401s, is treated as a miss, and the catalog rung silently never fires — no log above debug.
gaps.proposed_test: tests/test_utility_slot.py: monkeypatch requests.get to capture headers; anchor endpoint api_key='tok'; assert the /api/tags request carries Authorization: Bearer tok.
gaps.proposed_fix: Send the same Bearer header on the Ollama path when api_key is non-empty (mirror client.py:527-528).

verdict.reason: ORIGIN VERIFIED: auxiliary_client.py:682-684 carries the comment 'Most /v1/models endpoints are authenticated; an anonymous 401 would read as no small model and pin the curated default forever', with tests/agent/test_auxiliary_client.py:4941-4958 (test_catalog_fetch_is_authenticated) pinning it. BUT the halbert_evidence is MISATTRIBUTED and the failure scenario cannot occur. client.py:527-528 is the PEER compute path (`{base}/api/compute/v1/chat/completions`, client.py:515) and client.py:568-569 is the OpenAI-compatible path -- neither is an Ollama call. Halbert's actual Ollama chat call, _call_ollama (client.py:695-758), sends NO headers at all and does not even accept an api_key; every other Ollama read in the tree is likewise anonymous: client.py:1009 (/api/tags context probe), utils/ollama.py:63/73/100, dashboard/routes/llm.py:515/690/917, dashboard/routes/settings.py:167-175, and dashboard/routes/compute.py:100-101, which explicitly returns empty headers for provider=='ollama' while adding Bearer for everything else. So behind a token-checking proxy chat itself would 401 first -- the gap's premise ('chat works; the utility probe 401s') is impossible, and the utility probe is consistent with the whole codebase. This is a cloud-catalog invariant (authenticated remote /v1/models) that does not transfer to a single local Ollama daemon. At most a one-line consistency nicety, not a gap.

gaps.title: A failing utility model is never rescued by the next rung / the chat floor at request time

gaps.halbert_evidence: integrations/speech_summarizer.py:116-136 (single call_llm_chat; any exception → return original text); model/utility_slot.py:93-106 (no way to ask the ladder for 'the next rung after X')

gaps.proposed_test: tests/test_speech_summarizer.py: resolver returns DECLARED small-a; call_llm_chat stub raises for model small-a and succeeds for the chat model; assert the summary is produced and the second call used the chat model. tests/test_utility_slot.py: _resolve_aux(exclude={('small-a','http://localhost:11434')}) skips the declared rung.
gaps.proposed_fix: Let _resolve_aux accept an `exclude` set of (model, url) and have the summarizer retry once with the ladder re-run excluding the failed pick (bounded by the same 12 s budget: e.g. 6 s + 6 s). Log at WARNING once per (model,url) per process when a declared utility model fails so the operator can see the slot is stale. Optionally have normalise warn when a declared utility model is absent from the endpoint's listing (only on the picker save path, never at read).

verdict.reason: ORIGIN VERIFIED: auxiliary_client.py:3826-3860 _try_main_agent_model_fallback is the last-resort fall back to the main agent provider+model after the configured chain is exhausted, with a failed-backend skip and a health check; :3138-3156 _is_model_not_found_error classifies the 404/'model not found' case; :6510-6535 walks the configured fallback chain and then the auto chain when the explicit provider is unavailable. HALBERT VERIFIED: speech_summarizer.py:116-136 makes exactly one call_llm_chat and returns the original text on any exception; utility_slot.py:93-147 offers no exclude/next-rung parameter; llm_config.normalise (llm_config.py:488-503) validates only endpoint existence and chat capability, so a declared-but-deleted utility model stays enabled. SEVERITY LOWERED to low: the failure is fail-soft by design and degrades exactly to the pre-C2 behaviour (the full reply is spoken); nothing is lost or leaked. The genuinely bad part -- that nothing above DEBUG says the slot is stale (speech_summarizer.py:108/111/135/142, utility_slot.py:122/143/160/180) -- is already carried by own-bug 'task provenance is documented but not implemented'.

And the probe is paid BEFORE that check (fetch at :177-181, anchor size test at :185-187), so the round-trip is spent for nothing on every long spoken reply on such a setup, on the event loop. capabilities.py:22 _SIZE_TAG_RE already accepts [:\-_], so Halbert owns the more permissive parser it needs.

halbert_own_bugs.title: Legacy rung is dead after the first store read in the process
halbert_own_bugs.evidence: model/utility_slot.py:115-117, 287-297 (legacy read happens before THIS resolution's first load, but the comment at 26-31 assumes it is the file's first load); llm_config.py:74-78 (small_model in DROPPED_KEYS), 545-549 (needs_migration true), 656-695 (load_global_file rewrites the file, popping small_model at 639-640). Any earlier llm_config.load()/resolve() in the process (e.g. the chat turn's own model resolution, which always precedes a spoken summary) has already migrated and rewritten the file, so _legacy_aux_entry() finds no small_model.
halbert_own_bugs.scenario: Operator with a pre-migration models.yml starts the server; the first chat turn resolves chat_model (migrating the file); the first long spoken reply then resolves the utility model → LEGACY never fires, CHAT does. tests/test_utility_slot.py:189-228 pass only because they call _resolve_aux before any store read. A test that calls store.load() first and then expects AuxSource.LEGACY would go red. Given the standing directive 'no back-compat shims — leave old data unread', the rung should probably be deleted rather than fixed.
halbert_own_bugs.verdict_reason: CONFIRMED. llm_config.small_model is in DROPPED_KEYS (llm_config.py:74-78); needs_migration returns True for it (:563-568 via DROPPED_KEYS); load_global_file (:657-697) calls _write_raw(out) on the migrated dict, and migrate_legacy pops every DROPPED_KEY at :639-640. The read path reaches that rewrite: utility_slot.py:120 -> llm_config.resolve (:909-921) -> load_file (:751-759) -> load_global_file. So any earlier resolution in the process (every chat turn resolves chat_model, and the summarizer only runs after a reply exists) has already rewritten the file without small_model, and utility_slot._legacy_aux_entry (:287-320) then reads a file that no longer has the key. tests/test_utility_slot.py:189-228 pass only because they call _resolve_aux first in a fresh tmp config dir. Given the standing 'no back-compat shims, leave old data unread' directive, deleting the rung is the cleaner resolution than fixing it.

halbert_own_bugs.title: Synchronous probe + summary run inside the async responding handler and stall the event loop

Fix: run summarize() in a thread (asyncio.to_thread / run_in_executor) from the state machine, keeping the deterministic gate first.

halbert_own_bugs.title: _same_family prefix rule fuses distinct families that share a >=3-char prefix
halbert_own_bugs.evidence: model/utility_slot.py:257-265 (`candidate.startswith(reference) or reference.startswith(candidate)` with _MIN_FAMILY_TOKEN=3 at line 87).

Overlaps with G3/G9; fix by matching on the size-stripped family token with an exact or dash-delimited-suffix rule.

A14-utility-slot-model.summary: Halbert's utility slot (model/utility_slot.py, D-7) faithfully ports the shape of Hermes's aux ladder — explicit declaration first, opt-in live-catalog rung, legacy dict, main-model floor, every rung fail-soft — and is stronger on two founder axes (no model names anywhere; the pick must be strictly cheaper than the anchor). The port is weaker than the origin on the operational invariants around the probe and the pick: the catalog fetch is uncached with no negative cache (Hermes memoises and negatively caches for 120 s), the opt-in is a code kwarg rather than an operator config knob (Hermes: auxiliary.<task>.prefer_fast_model default False; OpenClaw: explicit-empty disables), only 'embed' is disqualified (Hermes excludes thinking/vision/tts/batch siblings), and a failing utility model is never rescued by the next rung. Two findings are Halbert-specific and matter most: (G4, high) the ladder and the speech summarizer never consult SEC-21 locality or the turn's secure_context, so a ':cloud' catalog sibling or a cloud-provider utility slot can receive the spoken copy of a secure turn; and (G9/own bug) the family/size parsers only understand Ollama's 'family:Nb' shape, so the rung is silently Ollama-only despite six listed OpenAI-wire providers. Own bugs: the legacy rung is unreachable in a running server (any prior store read migrates the file) and arguably violates the 'leave old data unread' directive; `task` provenance is documented but never logged; the sync probe+summary runs inline in the async responding handler and stalls the event loop; loader.py uses yaml without importing it. No changes were made to any repo.

halbert_own_bugs.title: Fixed 1-second race between the delayed scheduler start and the proactive-job registration thread
halbert_own_bugs.verdict_reason: CONFIRMED from dashboard/app.py:1234-1263 and 1267-1315. Both threads are created in the same startup block (scheduler_starter.start() around 1262, proactive_starter.start() at 1315), so they begin within microseconds. start_scheduler_delayed sleeps 3 s (1236) then constructs AutonomousExecutor(max_workers=3, ...) (1252-1257) — __init__ loads the autonomy guardrail YAML (executor.py:180-186), constructs SchedulerEngine which os.listdir + json.loads every per-job record (engine.py:27-40), and loads receipts.json and restarts.json — before assigning the module global and calling start(). schedule_proactive_jobs_delayed sleeps 4 s (1270) then does 'if executor is None: logger.info("Scheduler not running; proactive jobs not scheduled"); return' (1272-1275). The whole handoff budget is one second, the failure is silent at info level, and the consequence is that no cron job is registered and no boot catch-up runs for the entire process lifetime. An Event (or bounded poll) is the correct handoff.

halbert_own_bugs.verdict_reason: CONFIRMED. app.py:456 calls _surface(~/.ssh, recursive=False) and _surface appends one line per entry with absolute path, size, octal mode and mtime (app.py:437-443). monitor_hash.py:179 stores output_text[:max_stored_bytes] (default 65536, monitor_hash.py:93) in self._outputs, and _flush (125-155) writes {'hashes','outputs'} to data_subdir('scheduler')/monitor_hashes.json — the plaintext ~/.ssh inventory is persisted solely so a later unified diff can be produced (monitor_hash.py:192). A15-heartbeat-catchup-wiring.refute_summary: 12 gaps checked against origin code and the whole Halbert core/tests/.handoff set; 9 stand, 3 refuted. Standing, in dispatch order: G1 (a served catch-up writes only to the `<id>:catchup` record while registration blanks the parent via engine.add_job's overwrite, so the same slot is re-served on every restart — verified end to end; lowered high->medium because the monitor-hash gate absorbs the detector_sweep repeats and the visible residue is a duplicate morning report per restart inside 12 h); G2 (occurrence idempotency has zero production callers and no UTC canonicalisation — the mechanism G1/G3 need, and the module docstring claims a guarantee it does not deliver); G5 (ticker liveness markers — origin-verified and explicitly ruled in by F-4 Option A, still unbuilt); G4 (no schedule-change guard although the prior record already carries str(cron_expr)); G3 (recovery and catch-up can arm the same job at boot — NOTE the audit's proposed `_boot_recovery_pending` guard is broken, executor.py:340 drains that set during registration; lowered to low since both runs are idempotent); G6/G7/G8/G9 at low (BaseException ends the tick task; stop does not join an in-flight sweep, contradicting app.py:1626-1628's own comment; failed slots treated as served forever; dormant retirement diagnostic). Refuted: G10 (skip-missed switch — OpenClaw needs it for arbitrary user job sets, Halbert's three jobs are already bounded, age-gated and gate-suppressed), G11 (the cited origin line is a deferred-stamp clock read rather than a stale-immediate-run guard, and the probe reduces to a ~/.ssh listdir on macOS because /etc/systemd/system and /etc/fstab do not exist, so 60 s cannot elapse), G12 (sequential/fenced catch-up is incidental here — 2 immediate runs on a 3-worker pool — and the proposed 5 s spacing is not in the origin; stagger.ts:11 is a 5-minute top-of-hour jitter). All 5 halbert_own_bugs confirmed, three with scope corrections: the :catchup/:recovery records are bounded to six files (status-count pollution, not disk growth); the satellite-guard divergence has a concrete trigger (canonical_thread_url set with no peer_token falls back to a local store at threads.py:1252-1257, so the tick sweeps while catch-up is skipped); and monitor_hashes.json is 0600 but the ~/.ssh listing is effectively its whole payload on macOS. The alternating-judge half also confirmed: circuit._reset() at :344 clears both counters on any clean verdict, so ok/garbage alternation never trips the parse breaker. There is no loop to run away today; the rail belongs with whichever caller lands, and putting turn counters inside JudgeCircuit fights the module's stated design.

A02-eval-harness.summary: The R5 harness ports the Hermes compaction-eval shape faithfully in three places (content-keyed question-bank invariance — stronger than Hermes's path-keyed cache; an always-present ceiling arm printed first; finish_reason=length as a never-stored failure) and the verdict contract ports gates-before-judge, the closed vocabulary, the evidence-demanding prompt and the parse/transport breaker split. The port is NOT as solid as the origin on the instrument's integrity: run_exam hands the answerer the gold answer (G1, high — the closed-book claim is only true for the built-in regex answerer), judge_score has no hedging check so any longer/negated/punctuated correct answer scores partial and the packet's own hedging-marker spec was dropped (G2), and there is no recovery arm although retrieval over receipts is Halbert's real production answer to a destroyed region (G3). The verdict module is a pure per-turn function with no consumer yet, and relative to goals.py it lacks the loop-level safety rails: gate output is head-bounded instead of tail-bounded (G4), a raising gate crashes the evaluator (G5), nothing ends a permanently failing gate or an ok/garbage-alternating judge (G6), the judge call has no timeout (G7), WAIT accepts pid<=0/seconds=0/no target (G8), breakers reset only on success and are inert when the caller omits the circuit (G9, G10). Confirmed Halbert-own bugs: render()/main() raise TypeError when an OK arm has zero questions; the gate-output truncation marker can never appear; exact-match punctuation fragility; non-PolicyFailed exceptions abort the whole matrix; dead ParseCircuitOpen/TransportCircuitOpen and _HEDGES symbols. None of the proposed fixes require a model in any decision or touch consolidation.py's flag; engine-side (Haloysius) implications: none — every file in this unit is Halbert-side.

gaps.proposed_test: tests/persona/test_admission_wiring.py: after POST /api/guest/private/assign succeeds, assert an admission receipt exists (receipt_id keyed by route+request, decisive_gate='guest_fronting', gate ids in order, claim/identity coverage field) in the audit sink; assert a second attempt to consume the same receipt is refused; assert a receipt older than the max age or from a previous process generation is rejected as 'unknown', not 'allowed'.

verdict.reason: ORIGIN VERIFIED by reading the code: admission-evidence.ts:76-77 (MAX_CONTRIBUTIONS=16, MAX_AGE_MS=30d), :199-226 recordChannelIngressResolution freezes a binding with handoff{consumed:false} for every resolved ingress, :383-385 'Consume before validation and before the ordinary context builder runs.' with binding.handoff.consumed=true, :516-528 activePayload rejects a payload whose generation != state.generation or whose age exceeds the bound, :599 state.consumedEvidence.add(evidence); admission-decision-receipt.ts:27-82 mints a DecisionReceiptV1 with receiptId, occurredAt, decision.outcome ('unknown' when coverage is unknown/unsupported), reasonCode, enforcement.policyRefs ['channel.identifier-authentication'] and the remediation 'Treat this receipt as diagnostic provenance, not authorization.'; runtime.ts:709-737 stamps identifierAuthentication affected/evaluated/not-evaluated onto the binding. HALBERT VERIFIED: dashboard/routes/guest.py:277-291 is the only consumer of the IngressDecision — it maps the decisive gate's facts['http_status'] onto the HTTPException and writes one logger.info on deny / logger.debug on dispatch, then the decision is dropped; persona/admission.py:48-53 IngressDecision has only (admission, decisive_gate, reason_code, gate_graph) — no id, timestamp, epoch, consumed flag or sink. A hash-chained audit log DOES exist (obs/audit.py:212 write_audit, AUDIT_EVENT_KIND='tool_execution' at :65) and is written by tools/base.py, autonomy/guardrails.py, persona/manager.py etc., but grep across the core finds no admission-decision writer and tools/executor.py:743-762 _audit records only tool/args/session/success/error. The code's own stated invariant is unmet: routes/guest.py:114-117 says 'a refusal answers with the decisive gate and its reason code, so any "no" can be explained after the fact' — after the fact there is only a log line. Citation drift: _REASON_TEXT/_deny_payload are at 129-138/158-163, not 118-128. Narrowing for dispatch: the once-consumed WeakMap + owner-epoch machinery exists in OpenClaw because ingress evidence crosses a plugin/gateway boundary in a multi-channel bot; on a single-process single-user host that half degenerates to a trivial in-process spent-set. The audit-receipt half (record the decision, fail closed to 'unknown' on epoch/age mismatch) is architecture-neutral and is the part worth building.

gaps.title: _admit evaluates every gate after the first block; later gates run on facts the earlier gate denied and can raise

The identity gate blocks (401) but the walk continues, _session_owned_gate raises AttributeError on peer.node_id, and the client gets a 500 with no decisive_gate/reason_code - exactly the opaque failure the packet set out to remove. Today the FastAPI dependency masks it on the three peer routes, so the seam is latent, not live.

verdict.reason: ORIGIN VERIFIED: decision.ts:319-327 returns on the first 'block-dispatch' route gate before any sender gate is constructed; :356-364 returns on a sender block before commandGate is built; :366-370 and :372-376 likewise for command and event — each phase is only constructed if every earlier phase allowed. HALBERT VERIFIED: dashboard/routes/guest.py:274-276 `for build in builders: gates.append(await build(request, peer, body))` runs EVERY builder, and persona/admission.py:56-68 only picks the first BLOCK out of the completed list. The audit's crash scenario is latent, as it admits: _session_owned_gate (guest.py:216-224) dereferences peer.node_id unguarded, but the three peer routes use Depends(require_peer_auth) (federation/peer_middleware.py:116-175) which RAISES 401 rather than returning None, so peer is never None in production. I FOUND A STRONGER, LIVE consequence the audit missed, which is why severity stays medium: on 'POST /api/guest/private/assign' (gates = _local_admin_gate, _guest_fronting_gate — guest.py:317) and 'POST /api/guest/forget' (:320), a request DENIED at the local-admin boundary still runs the second builder, which calls guest.current_guest() (guest.py:242, :251) — and current_guest() is not read-only: at guest.py:344-362 it can fire the session keepalive, an outbound HTTP request to the sibling home (persona/sibling.py:59, TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_S=3.0), and at :360/:372 it can end the session and notify observers. halbert_own_bugs.title: Claim derivation failure on a voice turn binds no claim, and 'no claim bound' means 'no cap' - the ladder fails open on its own exception path

halbert_own_bugs.verdict_reason: CONFIRMED as a fail-open direction, with the escalation scenario narrowed to unreachable-today. Verified: agents/state_machine.py:594-600 (voice branch — turn_identifier_claim=None, claim_from_source inside try/except logged at DEBUG as 'non-fatal'), :620-623 claim_strength_label collapses to 'none', :631-637 the ContextVar is set only `if turn_identifier_claim is not None` — and that bind is ITSELF inside a try/except, a second fail-open the audit did not name; tools/executor.py:557-567 `turn_claim = current_turn_claim.get(); if turn_claim is not None: effective_role = effective_voice_role(...)` — otherwise the stated role reaches RoleGate uncapped. The origin contrast holds: identifier-authentication.ts:12 and :31-38 floor an absent claim to 'asserted'/'mutable' rather than leaving a subject strengthless. WHAT I COULD NOT CONFIRM is the exploit: the cap only matters with speaker_role='admin', and the shipped voice door (dashboard/routes/agent.py:1795-1803) only stamps a role from a receipt whose verified flag is set (dashboard/voice_relay.py:199-206), which yields claim_source='voice_speaker_verification' = ASSERTED, where the cap is a no-op anyway; the other voice entry points pass speaker_role='unknown' explicitly (integrations/wyoming_agent.py:256, audio/pipeline.py:568), and with no role state_machine.py:551-560 defaults voice to the channel's 'unknown'. So the fail-open cannot currently be reached with an admin role. Real as a fail-direction and as a mislabelled 'non-fatal' comment; dispatch as low-severity fail-closed hardening (bind IdentifierClaim(strength=UNVERIFIED) on the voice branch; cap whenever current_turn_channel is voice and no claim is bound), not as a live privilege escalation.

halbert_own_bugs.title: The keepalive network round trip runs while offer()/heartbeat()/withdraw() hold the module RLock
halbert_own_bugs.evidence: persona/guest.py:347-352 comment 'Outside the lock: this may be a network round trip' is true only for a bare current_guest() call; :400-401 offer(), :431-432 heartbeat(), :446-447 withdraw() all call current_guest(now) inside `with _lock:` (an RLock, so the nested `with _lock` at :338 does not release it). sibling.py:44 TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_S = 3.0 bounds the call; _notify (:361, :373) also runs under the outer lock in those paths.
halbert_own_bugs.scenario: A pulled session (keepalive=client.ping) is past its deadline when a paired app POSTs /api/guest/offer. offer() takes the lock, current_guest() starts the ping, the home is asleep, and for up to 3 s every other reader - the Presence Pill's poll on GET /api/guest, the agent prompt builder's current_guest() read, the heartbeat route - blocks on _lock. Fix: in current_guest(), if the lock is already held by this thread (or restructure offer/heartbeat/withdraw to read `_session` directly under the lock and end an expired session without renewing), skip the keepalive and treat the session as expired for the mutating caller; or perform the keepalive before taking the lock in the mutating paths.
halbert_own_bugs.verdict_reason: CONFIRMED by reading persona/guest.py. _lock is threading.RLock() (:302), so the nested `with _lock:` at :338 and the re-acquisitions at :355 and :363 never release the outer lock. current_guest()'s comment at :347-349 ('Outside the lock: this may be a network round trip') is true only for a bare top-level call; offer() takes the lock at :400 and calls current_guest(now) at :401, heartbeat() at :431-432, withdraw() at :446-447 — all three therefore run keep() (:352) and _notify() (:361, :373) while holding the module lock. Bounded by persona/sibling.py:44 TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_S=3.0 via the requests timeout at :59. During that window every other reader blocks: GET /api/guest, the prompt builder's current_guest(), the heartbeat route. Additionally _notify (:325-330) invokes arbitrary observer callbacks under the lock on those paths, widening the window beyond the transport timeout. Of the two proposed fixes, restructuring offer/heartbeat/withdraw to read _session directly is the cleaner one — those callers want the expiry verdict, not a renewal.

halbert_own_bugs.title: persona_id is interpolated into the sibling URL path without escaping
halbert_own_bugs.evidence: persona/sibling.py:126 `url = self.home.base_url + path.format(pid=self.home.persona_id)`; persona/guest.py:242-244 persona_id is only required to be one line of <=120 chars (no '/', '?', '#' rejection); guest_homes.py:234-236 the id may come from the remote home's own listing.
halbert_own_bugs.scenario: A sibling home (or anything answering on its port) lists a persona with id 'marnie/../../admin/export?x=' ; 'be Marnie' then sends Halbert's bearer token in a GET/POST to a path on that host that the home's API never intended, and every later memory_add/memory_search for the session (sibling.py:171, 182) goes there too. Same-origin, so the blast radius is the home itself, but Halbert should not be steerable by the data it fetched. Fix: urllib.parse.quote(persona_id, safe='') in _call, and reject '/', '?', '#' in GuestHome.from_payload.
halbert_own_bugs.verdict_reason: CONFIRMED. persona/sibling.py:125-126 `url = self.home.base_url + path.format(pid=self.home.persona_id)` with no quoting, feeding _headers() at :119-123 which attaches `Authorization: Bearer <home token>`; every later call for the session goes through the same _call (list_personas :138, fetch_persona :144, ping :153, memory_add :171, memory_search :182). Input side as described: persona/guest.py:242-244 requires only a non-empty one-line value of <=120 chars ('/', '?', '#', '..' all pass), and guest_homes.py:234-237 takes the id straight out of the REMOTE home's listing response (`pid = str(entry.get('id') or entry.get('persona_id') or '').strip()`) with no character check. So a home — or anything answering on its port — can steer the path Halbert sends its bearer token to. Same-origin, so the blast radius is that home's own API (low is right), but urllib.parse.quote(persona_id, safe='') plus a reject-on-'/?#' in from_payload is a two-line fix.

A12-claims-admission.summary: The port is faithful where it was scoped: the four-rank ladder, the >= floor, fail-closed defaults (stronger than the origin's 'asserted' default), raw-id hashing, the decision record shape, first-block-wins, and fail-closed-on-unwritten-policy (with a registry-completeness pin the origin lacks) are all in persona/claims.py, persona/admission.py and routes/guest.py, and the channel-ceiling clamp is a genuine strengthening. What is not as solid as the origin: (1) decisions are discarded after the HTTP response - there is no once-consumed evidence binding or audit receipt (G1); (2) the ladder has exactly one consumer with one hard-coded threshold (voice_role_ceiling) and meets_floor is dead code - no capability can declare a claim floor (G2); (3) _admit evaluates every gate after a block, so later gates run on denied facts and can 500 (G3); (4) SKIP/OBSERVE effects are advertised but dispatch (G4); (5) the main talk door (channel resolve, relay receipt, stamp) never walks decide_ingress and ChannelRefused hand-copies the payload shape (G6); (6) evaluated/affected diagnostics and a closed reason-code set are missing (G5, G7). Pairing-required/challenge-code enrollment is deliberately deferred (packet-02 C3) and does not apply to a single-user host. The most important Halbert-own defect is on the claims consumption path: any exception in claim derivation on a voice turn binds no claim, and the executor equates 'no claim bound' with 'typed turn, no cap' - the ladder fails open on its own error path (state_machine.py:594-600, executor.py:559-561), where the origin floors an absent claim to unverified. Secondary own bugs: the keepalive network call runs under the module RLock from offer/heartbeat/withdraw; the local-admin predicate accepts the 'testclient'/'localhost' sentinels; persona_id is path-interpolated unescaped; the 'home:' owner namespace is not fenced from operator-chosen peer ids; guest_homes.yml is renamed without fsync. Engine-side (Haloysius) implication: none for this unit - the warrant type is consumed, not gated, and the packet's composition rule (ladder never chained into warrant.authorize) is honoured in code and docstrings.

halbert_own_bugs.verdict_reason: Reproduced with arch -arm64 .venv/bin/python: 5 recalls of one query (score 0.8) persist as recall_count=5; reopening the same DB yields recall_count=1, avg 0.8; one more recall at score 0.2 yields recall_count=2, avg_score=0.5 instead of 0.7. halbert_own_bugs.title: Second connection to state_ledger.db without the StateStore durability/secure-delete PRAGMAs
halbert_own_bugs.evidence: promotion.py:149-151 (busy_timeout, WAL only) vs state_store.py:311-324 (secure_delete=ON, darwin checkpoint_fullfsync=1, synchronous=FULL, documented as 'platform truth, not preference')
halbert_own_bugs.scenario: The same file is written under two durability regimes; a shutdown that the StateStore guards against can corrupt the promotion tables' last checkpoint. Low impact (hash-only data) but inconsistent with the store-hardening packet's ruling.
halbert_own_bugs.verdict_reason: Confirmed with one correction. Measured on a store opened by promotion.py:148-151: secure_delete=0, checkpoint_fullfsync=0, journal_mode=wal, busy_timeout=5000, synchronous=2. state_store.py:309-324 sets secure_delete=ON and, on darwin, checkpoint_fullfsync=1 and synchronous=FULL, commented 'Platform truth, not preference -- not config-gated'. Both connections address the same file (~/.local/share/halbert/state_ledger.db). Real but low: promotion never deletes rows, so the secure_delete divergence has nothing to leave in slack today; the checkpoint_fullfsync divergence applies whenever the promotion connection auto-checkpoints the shared WAL.

A01-promotion.summary: Halbert's port (continuity/promotion.py, wired at threads.py:355-360 and recall_memory.py:239-243) faithfully lifts the origin's *shape* — usage-fact signals, hashed queries, distinct-day recurrence, count/diversity gates, fail-soft persistence, signals only for surfaced evidence — and is stronger in one respect (it stores no content at all). It is materially weaker on the mechanics that make the origin's ranking trustworthy, and it has no consumer. Verified against OpenClaw code (short-term-promotion-{record,utils,store,apply}.ts, short-term-promotion.ts, memory-workspace-lock.ts, dreaming.ts, tools.ts, memory-forget.ts) and by a scratchpad reproduction: (1) rank_candidates is called by nothing and the Consolidator never reads the store, so 'memory graduates because it was useful' is not yet true (G1, high); (2) recency is a record-time snapshot that never ages, so decay is a no-op on production data (G2, high); (3) persisted recall_count is discarded on reload and replaced by the distinct-query count, corrupting the running average (G3, medium); (4) no origin class — guest/private turns and ACTOR_SYSTEM facts earn signals where the origin blocks untrusted/system before scoring (G4); (5) forget_request never reaches the promotion tables and ERASURE_LIMITS does not name them (G5); (6) nothing is bounded or clamped — diversity can dominate the score and the tables grow forever (G6); (7) gates are weaker: no min score, no max age, diversity 2-on-queries vs 3-on-max(queries, days) (G7). Lower-severity gaps: dead recall-loop guard (G8), no event journal (G9), cross-process last-writer-wins on counts (G10), un-normalized query hashing (G11), fragile load path (G12), no dangling-key audit (G13), relevance weight zero (G14). Phase-signal boosts (G15) and the LanceDB timeout/cooldown rails do not apply. The apply side (promotedAt idempotency, marker reconciliation, budget compaction, plan-based consolidation) is deliberately gated as Phase B/C by packet 01 and is reported as adapted, not missing. All fixes are deterministic and Halbert-side; no engine (Haloysius) change is implied, though the packet's Phase C note about claim-keyed signals should be revisited because the thread site keys on a row id ('thread:<id>').

verdict.reason: ORIGIN: hermes-agent/tui_gateway/tool_progress.py:21-35 — _cap_tui_verbose_text takes start = max(line_start, len-MAX_CHARS), advances to the next newline when start > line_start ('never mid-line'), and builds the header from BOTH counts ('{lines} lines / {chars} chars', else '{chars} chars'). gaps.title: Window set lives for the process and is bounded per window, not per value: one large note can evict every earlier secret

gaps.proposed_fix: Store windows per value with a per-value cap (e.g. stride-sampled windows beyond 512) and a value-level FIFO; optionally forget a value when its egress ack TTL lapses.

verdict.reason: ORIGIN: openclaw/src/gateway/boot.ts:142 sets the echo context before the agent run and :163 clears it in the finally; boot-echo-guard.ts:66-75 drops the cached chunk set for that normalized prompt on clear, so the window store is bounded by run lifecycle rather than a global count. HALBERT: security/echo_guard.py:60-63,90-96 keeps ONE OrderedDict FIFO of 16384 windows across all values, popitem(last=False) per insert; grep over halbert_core/ and tests/ shows no production caller of EchoGuard.clear_session (tests only, plus the unrelated model/config_layers.py:217 clear_session), and the injection site (config/queries.py:357-360) has no scope to clear. halbert_own_bugs.evidence: agents/state_machine.py:3795-3803 and agents/turn_event_tee.py:69-80 hard-code "redacted": True before calling registry.redact_text, which may be a no-op (see G1 repro)

Verified by running the two modules in isolation (arch -arm64 .venv/bin/python, scratchpad/wf-oss/repro_a05.py): for a partial echo (85 of a 90-char acked value) find_match returns an 80-char window while redact_text returns the text unchanged — the warning asserts a redaction that did not occur. halbert_own_bugs.title: Streaming draft crosses the wire and renders before the guard runs
halbert_own_bugs.evidence: agents/state_machine.py:3955-3956 and :3980 yield response_chunk raw; the guard runs at :4018 on the committed text and the comment at :4008-4016 calls the drafts transient; frontend hooks/useAgentStream.ts:567-572 appends chunks live and :640-654 replaces the bubble only on response_complete
halbert_own_bugs.scenario: The model streams the acked secret token by token; it is visible in the bubble (and on any second screen mirroring the SSE) for the whole generation, then replaced. OpenClaw's guard runs before any dispatch (message-tool-visible-content.ts:338-398).
halbert_own_bugs.verdict_reason: agents/state_machine.py:3953-3955 and :3979 yield StreamEvent.response_chunk with the raw model text; the guard runs only at :4018 on the committed text, and the comment at :4008-4016 states this is deliberate ('a transient draft the frontend replaces'). The frontend confirms the exposure window: dashboard/frontend/src/hooks/useAgentStream.ts:567-568 appends every chunk live and :640-655 replaces the bubble only on response_complete, which does carry the clean text (state_machine.py:4246-4248). So an acked secret renders token-by-token for the whole generation and is then swapped out — visible on screen and to any SSE mirror. Confirmed as behaviour and as a real (transient) exposure; note it is a documented design choice, so the founder is being asked to revisit a decision rather than fix a slip.

halbert_own_bugs.title: Short-value whole-text match contradicts the documented 80-char floor
halbert_own_bugs.evidence: security/echo_guard.py:74-79 `max(1, len(norm) - window + 1)` yields the whole text as one chunk; repro: note 'abcd9876' then scan_outbound('abcd9876') is True while 'the token is abcd9876' is False; tests/test_echo_guard_wiring.py:213-237 documents the floor
halbert_own_bugs.scenario: A one-word reply that happens to equal a short acked value is flagged and passed through the registry (which redacts it); harmless but the floor the tests describe does not hold.
halbert_own_bugs.verdict_reason: The behaviour reproduces exactly (note_injected('abcd9876'); scan_outbound('abcd9876') True, scan_outbound('the token is abcd9876') False), but it is not a defect: security/echo_guard.py:74-79 states it in the code ('a text shorter than the window contributes its whole self as a single chunk (and a scan of text shorter than the window compares whole-to-whole the same way)'), and tests/test_echo_guard_wiring.py:223-237 pins the boundary with a docstring naming the whole-text chunk explicitly. The only effect is that a reply which is exactly the short acked value gets flagged and registry-redacted — the desired outcome. No failure scenario; at most a wording nit in the invariant table.

halbert_own_bugs.title: One oversized note evicts every earlier value's windows
halbert_own_bugs.evidence: security/echo_guard.py:57-63,91-96 single FIFO of windows across values, popitem(last=False) per insert beyond 16384
halbert_own_bugs.scenario: Acking a 20 KB key after three API keys leaves the API keys unguarded (G11).
halbert_own_bugs.verdict_reason: security/echo_guard.py:60-63 holds one OrderedDict FIFO across all values with _max_chunks=16384 and :94-96 evicts the oldest window per insert. Reproduced: note a 100-char value (21 windows, scan_outbound True), then note a 17000-char high-entropy value -> the store saturates at 16384 and the first value's scan_outbound is False. With no production caller of clear_session anywhere (grep over halbert_core/ and tests/), earlier secrets stay unguarded until process restart. Same finding as G11.

halbert_own_bugs.title: Both caps firing produce a header that names only the omitted lines

halbert_own_bugs.scenario: A 20 x 2000-char output reports '[omitted 4 lines]' while ~31 KB of the kept lines were dropped silently (G8).
halbert_own_bugs.verdict_reason: security/display_transport.py:58-64: after dropping lines, body[-max_chars:] is applied unconditionally but the header is chosen by 'if omitted_lines else', so the char cut is never named when a line cut also fired.
